title: Buna: The Sound of Patience
logline: A grandchild remembers the morning coffee ceremony at their grandmother's house, and the patience it quietly taught.
audience: My family and followers in Ethiopia and the diaspora, watching on a phone, who know the ceremony and may be far from home.
intent: They should feel warmth and homesickness, and recognise patience and welcome as the real gifts of the ceremony.

language.tts_voice_style: Calm, warm, unhurried, like a grown grandchild remembering quietly.

style_block: Warm hand-painted gouache illustration, soft film grain, earthy palette of terracotta, cream, deep green and coffee brown, golden morning light, gentle depth of field, vertical composition with the subject centered.
negative_block: no text, no letters, no logos, no photorealistic faces, no extra fingers

character.name: Grandmother
character.description: An elderly Ethiopian woman in a white cotton habesha kemis with a thin woven border and a light netela on her shoulders, grey hair partly covered, always seen from behind, in profile or in silhouette, never facing the camera.

shots.reason: Establishes the place and the hour: a quiet courtyard house before sunrise.
shots.image_prompt: A small whitewashed courtyard house with a tin roof and a tall eucalyptus tree at first light, pale mist on the ground, one warm lit doorway.
shots.motion_prompt: Mist drifts slowly across the ground, the doorway light flickers gently.

narration.text_native: በአያቴ ቤት ሁልጊዜ ቀኑ የሚጀምረው ፀሐይ ሳትወጣ ነው።
narration.text_en: At my grandmother's house, the day always began before the sun.

shots.reason: The grass on the floor is the first sign of welcome and the first image of the ritual.
shots.image_prompt: Close view of fresh green grass and small yellow flowers spread over a clay floor, a low wooden stool and a tray of small white cups just visible at the edge.
shots.motion_prompt: A few blades of grass sway slightly, soft light moves across the floor.

narration.text_native: አዲስ ሳር ወለሉ ላይ ትጎዘጉዛለች። «እንኳን ደህና መጣችሁ» የምትለው በዚህ መንገድ ነው።
narration.text_en: She spreads fresh grass on the floor. It is how she says: you are welcome here.

shots.reason: Roasting is the moment the neighbourhood smells the coffee; it sets the senses of the film.
shots.image_prompt: Green coffee beans turning dark brown on a black flat roasting pan over glowing charcoal, thin smoke rising.
shots.motion_prompt: Smoke rises and curls slowly, the charcoal glows and dims.

narration.text_native: ጥሬ ቡና በብረት በምጣድ ላይ ይቆላል። ጭሱ ሲነሳ ሰፈሩ ሁሉ ቡና እንደሚመጣ ያውቃል።
narration.text_en: Green beans go onto the pan. Smoke rises, and the whole street knows coffee is coming.

shots.reason: Introduces the grandmother once, from behind, carrying the smoke slowly: patience in her movement.
shots.image_prompt: The grandmother seen from behind, walking slowly through a dim warm room carrying a roasting pan with rising smoke toward low stools.
shots.motion_prompt: She moves slowly forward, the smoke trails behind her.

narration.text_native: ጭሱን በክፍሉ ውስጥ በዝግታ ታዞራለች። እዚህ ምንም ነገር በችኮላ አይደረግም።
narration.text_en: She carries the smoke around the room, slowly. Nothing here is ever rushed.

shots.reason: Grinding is the rhythm shot: it gives the score a pulse and the narrator a childhood memory.
shots.image_prompt: A wooden mortar and a long iron pestle with dark roasted beans, a white sleeve just visible at the edge of the frame.
shots.motion_prompt: The pestle rises and falls slowly in a steady rhythm, a few beans shift.

narration.text_native: ከዚያ ቡናው በእጅ ይወቀጣል። ምቶቹን እቆጥር ነበር።
narration.text_en: Then the beans are ground by hand. I used to count the strokes.

shots.reason: The jebena on the charcoal is the emotional centre: waiting is the lesson.
shots.image_prompt: A black clay jebena with a long neck on glowing charcoal, steam curling from its spout, soft morning light from a doorway.
shots.motion_prompt: Steam curls up from the spout, the charcoal glows softly.

narration.text_native: ጀበናው በከሰል እሳት ላይ ይታዳል። እንጠብቃለን። መጠበቅ የቡናው አካል ነው።
narration.text_en: The clay pot sits on the charcoal. We wait. Waiting is part of the coffee.

shots.reason: The long steady pour shows her skill and calm; it is the visual peak of the ritual.
shots.image_prompt: A clay jebena pouring a thin stream of coffee into a row of small white cups on a tray, steam rising, warm light.
shots.motion_prompt: A thin steady stream flows into the cups, steam rises gently.

narration.text_native: ቡናውን በአንድ ረጅም ቀጭን መስመር ትከዳዋለች፤ አንድ ጠብታም አይፈስም።
narration.text_en: She pours in one long, thin line, and not one drop spills.

shots.reason: Neighbours arriving in silhouette shows the ceremony as community, not just coffee.
shots.image_prompt: A warm room with incense smoke curling in golden light, the grandmother seated in profile at the tray, two or three neighbours as soft silhouettes arriving at the doorway.
shots.motion_prompt: Incense smoke curls through the light, a silhouette steps slowly into the doorway.

narration.text_native: ጎረቤቶች አንድ በአንድ ይመጣሉ። ማንም ለምን እንደመጣ አይጠይቅም። የእጣን ጭስ ግብዣ ነው።
narration.text_en: Neighbours come, one by one. Nobody asks why. The smoke of frankincense is the invitation.

shots.reason: Three cups and three rounds give the story its structure and the motif of blessing.
shots.image_prompt: Three small white cups of coffee in a row on a tray with a few popcorn kernels, the light warmer and softer from left to right.
shots.motion_prompt: Steam rises from all three cups, the light shifts gently from cool to warm.

narration.text_native: ሦስት ዙር ነው። የመጀመሪያው አቦል፣ ሁለተኛው ቱና፣ ሦስተኛው በረካ።
narration.text_en: Three rounds. The first abol, the second tuna, the third bereka.

shots.reason: A quiet silhouette in the doorway light closes the memory and returns to the opening mood.
shots.image_prompt: The grandmother in silhouette in a bright doorway, steam from a jebena in the foreground, golden morning light flooding the room.
shots.motion_prompt: Light brightens slowly, the steam drifts up and fades.

narration.text_native: ከዚያ ወዲህ ብዙ ተምሬያለሁ። ግን የትዕግስትን ድምፅ አሁንም አውቀዋለሁ፤ በጸጥታ የምትዘምር ጀበና።
narration.text_en: I have learned much since. But I still know the sound of patience: a clay pot, quietly singing.

music.caption: Slow warm instrumental, solo krar lyre with soft hand percussion and a quiet drone, gentle Ethiopian pentatonic mood, intimate and unhurried, no strong lead melody under speech.

cues.purpose: Quiet drone and sparse notes: early morning, anticipation.
Gentle pulse from the krar and soft percussion, matching grinding and pouring.
Theme returns warmer and slower, then resolves into near silence.

end_card.text_en: made by mahlet. A family story.
